Implementation Plan Issue #10077 (re-issue of #9853 / #9821): implementation plan Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `dbd357487ae7e1cbcf3f64c41d30328c327966e1`, symbolic branch `main` (resolved checkout ref `main`). The "Integration branch mismatch" line reads `unknown`, not `true`. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` - `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` - `agents.d/10077-stall-escalate-human-comment.md` (new) - `changelog.d/10077-stall-escalate-human-comment.md` (new) ## Acceptance ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py::test_stall_escalate_human_comment_posted_after_judge_escalation red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py::test_stall_escalate_human_comment_skipped_when_label_unconfirmed ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py::test_stall_escalate_human_comment_write_failure_is_logged_and_nonfatal red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: this changes poller shell logic and tests only, and the PR's CI covers it; no deploy or release workflow depends on it. ## Automation / wiring (§20.E) - No new script. This only extends the existing `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. - Entry point: the existing scheduled poller (`.github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml`, cron and dispatch), through `recover_stalled_issue`, `invoke_stall_judge` and then `execute_stall_recovery_action`. No new wiring is needed. - No new long-running supervisor. No database work. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`. - No new environment variable that workflows set. `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION` is a process-internal global, set and unset in the same function. When it is unset, the reason falls back to the default sentence (§8). ## Functions or modules to implement 1. **New helper `_post_stall_escalate_human_comment `** in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, placed just above `execute_stall_recovery_action()` (currently around line 22573, right after the automation-path hold-comment helper). The name is unique: a grep finds no `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN` or `_post_stall_escalate_human_comment` anywhere in the script. - Check `issue` against `^[0-9]+$`. If it fails, log `outcome=write_failed` and return 0. - **Source:** - `stall_judge` when `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION` is set, tested with `${STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION+x}`. Testing whether it is set, not whether it is empty, keeps an empty judge justification labelled as the judge. - `stall_recovery` otherwise. - **Reason:** `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION` when it is non-empty, otherwise `Stall recovery ran out of automatic actions for this phase.` - Neutralise every `` in the reason before rendering, because the judge's justification is model output. - **Body, in this order:** - The heading `## Stall recovery: human input needed`. - The reason line. - A line like `Stuck in \`\` for m.` The `` argument exists for this line; it is harmless context. - When `local_id` is non-empty and `TRACKING_NUM` matches `^[0-9]+$`: a pointer `Tracking issue: #`. - The resume step: `To resume, fix the blocker, then remove \`ai:needs-human\`.` - The last line, the marker: ``. - **Post:** follow the representative pattern already in this file (the automation-path hold comment helper just above, and the direct-issue branch of the judge comment): `gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${issue}/comments" -f body="${body}" >/dev/null 2>&1`. - **Log exactly one line on stdout:** `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_COMMENT issue= phase=

source=stall_judge|stall_recovery outcome=posted|write_failed`. - **Always `return 0`.** A failed write never changes the recovery result. 2. **`escalate_human)` arm** of `execute_stall_recovery_action` (around line 23488). Inside the existing `if has_label "${escalated_labels}" "ai:needs-human"; then` branch, after the CRITICAL `tg_notify`, add: `_post_stall_escalate_human_comment "${issue_num}" "${phase}" "${stall_minutes}" "${local_id}" || true` - The `else` branch (label not confirmed) stays as it is and posts no comment. 3. **Judge dispatch arm** of `invoke_stall_judge`, the first `case "${effective_action}"` arm (`retrigger_pipeline|...|escalate_human|skip)`, around line 25127). Replace `execute_stall_recovery_action ...; return $?` with: - `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION="${judge_justification}"` - `local _judge_dispatch_rc=0`. The name is unique in the file: a grep returns 0 matches. - `execute_stall_recovery_action "${issue_num}" "${phase}" "${effective_action}" "${recovery_count}" "${local_id}" "${stall_minutes}" || _judge_dispatch_rc=$?` - `unset STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION` - `return "${_judge_dispatch_rc}"` - The other arms (`resolve_merge_conflict`, fallback, `*`) are unchanged. Their escalations log `source=stall_recovery`. 4. **No other edits** to the script (the issue says "Change nothing else"). ## Data structures affected - A new issue-comment marker: ``. Nothing reads it yet; it exists for audit and for future dedupe. - A new global, `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION`. It is set only for the duration of one call to `execute_stall_recovery_action` from the judge arm. - No change to the state JSON or to labels. ## API or interface changes - One new stable log prefix: `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_COMMENT`, registered in the agents.d fragment. - One extra GitHub REST call (POST issue comment) per confirmed `escalate_human`. It fires only after the label is confirmed, so at most once per escalation, never in a loop. - §14 audit: the existing tracking-issue judge comment goes to `TRACKING_NUM`, not to the stalled issue, so no existing call can carry this body. Failure modes: - **Comment POST fails** (rate limit, 5xx). Symptom: `outcome=write_failed` in the log; the label and the CRITICAL Telegram alert still go out. Recovery: none needed, because the label is the real gate and the helper returns 0. - **Label not confirmed.** Symptom: the existing `::warning::` line; no comment is posted. Recovery: the existing bounded retry ladder. - **Judge justification is empty.** Symptom: the fallback reason appears with `source=stall_judge`. ## Decisions ### D1 — Source detection by whether the variable is set - Chosen: `source=stall_judge` when `STALL_ESCALATE_HUMAN_JUSTIFICATION` is set (`${VAR+x}`); the judge arm clears it with `unset`. - Alternatives considered: test for a non-empty value; add a second flag variable. - Why: an empty judge justification is still a judge escalation. A second variable would go beyond the spec's set/clear contract. ### D2 — Fragment file names use this issue's number - Chosen: `agents.d/10077-stall-escalate-human-comment.md` and `changelog.d/10077-stall-escalate-human-comment.md`, with "#9821" (and "Refs #9853") in the text. - Alternatives considered: `9821-` names, as the original PR used. - Why: this issue's number is always in scope for the plan approval gate. The spec's "fragments for 9821" is satisfied by the content. ### D3 — Comment posting pattern - Chosen: post with `gh_retry gh api .../issues//comments -f body=`, like the neighbouring automation-path hold helper. - Alternatives considered: `post_issue_comment_json` (it has file-payload and response handling). - Why: this is the same pattern as the closest representative, `-f body=` takes no shell interpolation, and the only result needed is success or failure. ### D4 — Neutralise HTML comment delimiters in the reason - Chosen: strip or replace `` in the justification before rendering. - Alternatives considered: render the reason verbatim. - Why: the judge output is untrusted model text. It must not be able to forge `ai:*` markers that other pollers read, such as the needs-human latch markers. This is a small, local change. ## Security considerations - **Trust boundaries.** Stall-judge output (model text) flows into a public issue comment. It is passed to `gh api` as an argument (`-f body=`), never through `eval` or into a shell string, and comment delimiters are neutralised (D4). Markdown in the reason is otherwise kept as is, the same as the existing judge comment already renders `judge_justification`. - **Authorization.** There is no new endpoint or surface. It uses the poller's existing `GH_TOKEN`, with no new permission. - **Abuse cases:** - A justification containing `` or a fake `ai:stall-escalate-human` marker. Mitigation: D4. - A very long justification. The judge output is already bounded by parsing, and the GitHub 65 KB comment limit causes `write_failed`, which is not fatal. - **Secrets.** None are logged; the log line carries only issue, phase, source and outcome. - **Money handling.** Not applicable. ## Potential risks or edge cases - **Conflict:** the spec says to use `git show isolated-base:scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` as the baseline, but in this snapshot `isolated-base` does not contain that file (likely filtered as oversized: `git diff isolated-base` shows the whole file as added). HEAD is `main` at `dbd3574`, so the working tree is the baseline. Line numbers above come from it. - **Possible duplicate comments.** An issue that is escalated, released by a human and escalated again gets a second comment. That is intended (one per confirmed escalation), and the marker allows dedupe later. - **Other readers of `ai:needs-human` text.** `release_head_bound_needs_human_latches` treats a later trusted comment mentioning `ai:needs-human` as a blocker, but it reads PR comments only.
